what: Converting a RefWorks or RIS export
title: Getting started with citelens
text: convert_refworks() reads RefWorks export returns BibTeX entries. accepts RefWorks Tagged Format (lines RT, A1, T1) RIS (lines TY  -, AU  -), detects one supplied. Citation keys built first author, year, first meaningful word title (example tinto2006research). letter added two keys otherwise collide. Reference types mapped BibTeX types (journal article article, book chapter incollection, thesis phdthesis, ); anything unrecognized becomes misc. write .bib file, give convert_refworks() output path:
code: ris <- system.file("extdata", "sample_refworks.ris", package = "citelens") entries <- convert_refworks(ris) cat(entries[1]) #> @article{tinto2006research, #>   author   = {Tinto, Vincent}, #>   title    = {{Research and practice of student retention: What next?}}, #>   journal  = {Journal of College Student Retention: Research, Theory \& Practice}, #>   year     = 2006, #>   volume   = {8}, #>   number   = {1}, #>   pages    = {1--19}, #>   issn     = {1521-0251}, #>   doi      = {10.2190/4NWK-STAC-2PLH-PJ3D}, #>   url      = {https://example.org/tinto2006}, #>   keywords = {retention, persistence}, #>   abstract = {This article reviews the last forty years of research on student retention and argues that institutions should focus on persistence in the classroom.} #> } bib_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".bib") convert_refworks(ris, bib_file) #> Converted 4 record(s) -> /tmp/RtmpFiksI8/file1a2b55f349ce.bib file.exists(bib_file) #> [1] TRUE

title: Getting started with citelens
text: bib_to_df() reads BibTeX file, whether came convert_refworks(), Google Scholar’s Cite > BibTeX option, another tool. result one row per entry. bibtype bibkey come first, followed one column every BibTeX field found file. Fields entry NA, every column character, convert year .integer() need arithmetic . default values cleaned: grouping braces removed ({{Title}} becomes Title), escapes \& undone, extra whitespace collapsed. what: Looking up missing abstracts in OpenAlex
title: Getting started with citelens
text: Text analytics need abstracts, Scholar’s results list none. fetch_abstracts() looks OpenAlex, DOI one title otherwise. OpenAlex requires free API key: Create free account https://openalex.org. Copy key https://openalex.org/settings/api. Save R. picked automatically afterward. examples send requests internet, run vignette built. fetch_abstracts() also works bib_to_df() table DOIs. sent. title (DOI) key sent OpenAlex, nothing else. careful matches. title match accepted titles close publication years agree within year. Otherwise abstract stays NA, missing abstract better wrong one. Many works OpenAlex abstract file, expect gaps. Diagnosing gaps. abstract_status column says happened reference: statuses found, abstract file, title matched, year differs, results, lookup failed. still-missing references retried run function result. columns abstract_match abstract_source help spot-check found. Usage limits. free key currently allows daily allowance credits, title lookup costs DOI lookup, thousand references fit day. allowance runs , function stops keeps found. Run later object picks left .
code: Sys.setenv(OPENALEX_API_KEY = "your-key")   # this session only # To keep it permanently, add OPENALEX_API_KEY=your-key to your .Renviron file. res <- scholar_parse_html("~/Downloads/scholar_page1.html") res <- fetch_abstracts(res)          # or fetch_abstracts(res, api_key = "your-key")  # the same, but straight to BibTeX with abstracts included scholar_html_to_bib("scholar_page1.html", "scholar.bib", abstracts = TRUE) table(res$abstract_status)  # titles that did not match, with the closest candidate found res[res$abstract_status == "title not matched",     c("title", "closest_title", "closest_score")]  # if the closest titles are the right papers, accept looser matches res <- fetch_abstracts(res, min_match = 0.75)  # "year differs": the title matched but the years are far apart # (re-editions, online-first dates) res[res$abstract_status == "year differs", c("title", "year", "closest_year")] res <- fetch_abstracts(res, max_year_diff = 10)

title: Topic modeling (LDA) of abstracts — topic_model
text: Text lower-cased, punctuation numbers removed, stop words (see [citelens_stopwords()]) short words dropped, simple plurals merged (students student count one word). Words occur fewer `min_doc_freq` abstracts ignored. Topic models need reasonably large collection (dozens abstracts ) give stable themes. handful abstracts output exploratory. Different `seed` values can give somewhat different topics; use [topic_k_search()] help choose `k`.

title: Topic modeling (LDA) of abstracts — topic_model
code: f <- system.file("extdata", "sample_abstracts.bib", package = "citelens") refs <- bib_to_df(f) filler <- c("note", "time", "follow", "shape", "touch", "studied", "evidence",             "work", "attention", "discussion")   # words from the synthetic sample m <- topic_model(refs, k = 3, stopwords = filler, seed = 1) m #> <citelens topic model> #> 3 topics from 30 abstracts (51 distinct words, 496 word occurrences) #> alpha = 1.67, beta = 0.01, sweeps = 1000 #>  #>  topic prevalence n_docs coherence #>      1        36%     10     -25.5 #>      2        33%     10     -27.2 #>      3        32%     10     -22.2 #>                                                                 top_terms #>                               college, cost, financial, aid, budget, debt #>  predictive, reporting, analytics, institutional, benchmarking, dashboard #>               retention, support, advising, attrition, dropout, mentoring topic_terms(m, n = 5) #>    topic rank          term       beta #> 1      1    1       college 0.07676292 #> 2      1    2          cost 0.07676292 #> 3      1    3     financial 0.07676292 #> 4      1    4           aid 0.07128377 #> 5      1    5        budget 0.07128377 #> 6      2    1    predictive 0.10036988 #> 7      2    2     reporting 0.10036988 #> 8      2    3     analytics 0.07529309 #> 9      2    4 institutional 0.07529309 #> 10     2    5  benchmarking 0.06902389 #> 11     3    1     retention 0.09652112 #> 12     3    2       support 0.09652112 #> 13     3    3      advising 0.08366021 #> 14     3    4     attrition 0.07722976 #> 15     3    5       dropout 0.07722976

title: Word trends over time — word_trends
text: data data frame one row per reference. words Words track, `c("equity", "belonging")`. `NULL`, `n` words found abstracts overall used. n Number words track `words` `NULL`. year Name column holding publication year. Text "2019" "Spring 2019" fine; first 4-digit number used. text Name column holding text analyse. bin Width period years (1 = one row per year). stopwords Extra words drop, addition [citelens_stopwords()]. min_word_length Drop words shorter many letters. singularize Merge simple plurals (default `TRUE`).

title: Word trends over time — word_trends
text: data frame `period` (first year period), `term`,   `n_docs` (abstracts mentioning ), `n_period` (abstracts period)   `share` (`n_docs / n_period`). Periods abstracts omitted.

title: Word trends over time — word_trends
text: Years abstracts give jumpy shares, check `n_period` (number abstracts year) reading much change. Use `bin` group years, example `bin = 5`.

title: Word trends over time — word_trends
code: f <- system.file("extdata", "sample_abstracts.bib", package = "citelens") refs <- bib_to_df(f) word_trends(refs, words = c("retention", "tuition"), bin = 5) #>   period      term n_docs n_period     share #> 1   2015 retention      7       18 0.3888889 #> 2   2020 retention      4       12 0.3333333 #> 3   2015   tuition      4       18 0.2222222 #> 4   2020   tuition      4       12 0.3333333
